noticing.title: Noticing changes?
noticing.subtitle: If you're wondering whether something is wrong, you're not alone. Many families start here.
noticing.p1_lead: Forgetting a name, repeating a question, getting confused in a new place — these can be normal aging or something more.
noticing.p2: What matters is that you noticed, and you're paying attention. That's the first act of care.
noticing.p3: The resources below can help you understand what you're seeing and decide whether to talk to a doctor. A doctor's visit is the only way to know for sure.
noticing.footnote: CalmGuide does not screen, diagnose, or assess cognitive function. We are an educational companion, not a medical tool.

diagnosis.title: Just received a diagnosis?
diagnosis.subtitle: This is one of the hardest moments. Take it one step at a time.
diagnosis.p1: A dementia diagnosis changes everything — and nothing — all at once. Your loved one is still the same person they were yesterday. But now you have a name for what's been happening, and that can feel like a lot.
diagnosis.p2_emph: You don't need to figure everything out today.
diagnosis.p2_tail: The most important thing right now is to breathe, and to know that millions of families have walked this road before you.
diagnosis.p3: The resources below connect you with people who can help you take the first steps — support groups, planning guides, and trained humans who understand.
diagnosis.p4: When you're ready, CalmGuide can help with the day-to-day: learning about the disease, coaching through tough moments, and caring for yourself along the way.

resources.helpline_desc: 1-800-272-3900 — Talk to a real person right now. They understand what you're feeling.
resources.support_desc: Connect with other families going through the same thing near you.

hospice.title: Thinking about hospice?
hospice.subtitle: This stage asks the hardest questions. You deserve support from people who have been here before.
hospice.p1: When dementia reaches its final stage, the focus shifts from managing behaviors to providing comfort. This is an entirely different kind of caregiving — and it deserves its own kind of support.
hospice.p2_emph: CalmGuide is not equipped to guide you through end-of-life decisions.
hospice.p2_tail: These decisions are deeply personal and medical, and they deserve the attention of hospice professionals, palliative care teams, and counselors who specialize in this stage.
hospice.p3: What we can tell you: choosing hospice is not giving up. It is choosing comfort and dignity for someone you love.

bereavement.title: After loss
bereavement.subtitle: The caregiving may be over, but the feelings aren't. That's normal.
bereavement.p1: Losing someone to dementia is a unique kind of grief. You may have been grieving for months or years before the death — watching the person you knew slowly change. Now that they're gone, the grief may feel different than you expected.
bereavement.p2: Relief, guilt, numbness, anger, sadness — all of these are normal. Often at the same time.
bereavement.p3_emph: CalmGuide was built for caregiving, not grief support.
bereavement.p3_tail: You deserve people who specialize in what you're going through now. The resources below can connect you.
bereavement.p4_lead: If the grief feels overwhelming or you're having thoughts of harming yourself, please call

resources.lifeline_desc: Call or text 988 — 24/7, free, confidential. If grief feels unbearable right now.
